findings: The neuroscience plan retains neural biology, perception and action, cognition and psychopathology, complemented by cellular and biochemical foundations, anatomy, laboratory methods, statistics, programming and machine learning. Neural Networks moves from term four to term six, exchanging places with Life Science Laboratory. Its statistics and mathematical prerequisites remain earlier. Current description-only Advanced Calculus provides differential-equation and multivariate methods and has been given its stated contribution. Perception & Action supports sensory processing and movement within its documented cognitive-neuroscience scope.

The population-health plan retains biomedical and health-psychology contributions with social research, economics, public health, communication and sustainability. A four-course rotation moves Introduction to Economics from term five to term one, Experimental Methods from term one to term five, Social Psychology from term six to term four, and Psychopathology from term four to term six. All formal prerequisites and offerings pass. Experimental Methods follows Social Psychology, and the economics foundation precedes Public Economics.

The first plan has a substantial brain and computation anchor. The second remains provisional and requires reconstruction or stronger justification because its population, policy and sociology emphasis may displace too much of the defining brain-science inquiry. Current external weighting and minor rules are required before resolving that academic question. Existing arts and philosophy candidates likewise need substantive assessment against a preserved brain-science core. Neither provisional plan is presented as an approved UCR option.
academicApproval: blocked by incomplete current external source evidence
